newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Escudo's ERM level suits Portugal performance - BoP.
newsitem.headline: Escudo's ERM level suits Portugal performance - BoP.

text.p: Bank of Portugal Governor Antonio de Sousa said the escudo's level within the European Union's Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM) reflected the performance of the Portuguese economy.

Sousa also said that the Portuguese economy was growing strongly and that the central bank may revise its forecast for Gross Domestic Product growth in 1997 towards the upper limit of a target range between 3.00 and 3.75 percent.
Asked if the escudo's level within the ERM was a true reflection of the performance of the Portuguese economy, Sousa told reporters: "I think so."
He noted that the Portuguese currency had remained stable within the ERM over the past four years.
The central rate of the escudo in the ERM is 197.398 per ecu and 102.5050 per mark.
At 1211 GMT, the escudo stood at 198.40/48 per ecu and 100.96/89 per mark.
Sousa, speaking after presenting the Bank of Portugal's annual report for 1996, said: "According to indicators until April, there is a quite elevated trend of growth in the economy."
He added: "This could lead to some revision (in the 1997 target range of between 3.0 and 3.75 percent), or probably point towards the upper end of the range."
He said it was premature now to revise the growth forecast and that a possible revision would take place in September, incorporating data from the first half of the year.
